expectations.text: Scope: all ePHI the organisation creates, receives, maintains, or transmits — across all systems, locations, and media, based on an asset/data inventory
expectations.evidence: "every system, application, and location that creates, receives, maintains, or transmits ePHI: EHR... email, laptops/mobile devices, backups/DR systems, cloud services... Inventory every ePHI-touching system/asset"

expectations.text: Process: identify threats and vulnerabilities, assess current safeguards, and rate likelihood and impact to derive risk levels
expectations.evidence: "Threat identification... Vulnerability identification... Likelihood assessment... Impact assessment... Risk level determination... Current controls inventory — what's already mitigating each risk"

expectations.text: Documentation and maintenance: the analysis must be documented and periodically reviewed/updated (after incidents, new systems, organisational change)
expectations.evidence: "Date it, version it, and set a review cadence (annually, and after any material system change, incident, or expansion). Retain documentation for 6 years (§164.316(b))"

expectations.text: Distinguishes a true risk analysis from a compliance checklist or gap assessment — a vendor checklist alone does not satisfy 164.308(a)(1)(ii)(A)
expectations.evidence: "A filled-in vendor checklist is almost certainly **not** a compliant risk analysis... 'we bought a checklist tool' is not a defense OCR accepts" vs §164.308(a)(1)(ii)(A) standard

expectations.text: Notes that a missing/inadequate risk analysis is OCR's most-cited failure in ransomware-related enforcement (Risk Analysis Initiative; 2026 self-funded plan settlements)
expectations.evidence: "the single most commonly cited deficiency in OCR enforcement actions, including two 2026 settlements against self-funded group health plan sponsors (Star Group L.P., $245K, and Spencer Gifts, $450K...)... discovered only after a ransomware incident"
